central_hazard_confirmations.workgroup_scope_barrier: CONFIRMED CORRECT. workgroup_barrier() lowers (crates/axc-codegen/src/subgroup.rs:285-301 emit_workgroup_barrier) to OpControlBarrier with EXECUTION scope = EXECUTION_SCOPE_WORKGROUP (=2) for BOTH the execution and memory scope operands, and MEMORY_SEMANTICS_WORKGROUP_ACQ_REL = 0x108 (AcquireRelease 0x8 | WorkgroupMemory 0x100). body.rs:576-585 maps HirStmt::Barrier{Workgroup} to exactly this. The unit test cg_workgroup_barrier_emits_op_control_barrier_with_scope_2_and_semantics_0x108 (subgroup.rs:476-519) asserts scope==2 and semantics==0x108. This is a WORKGROUP barrier (NOT a subgroup barrier — there is no subgroup-scope barrier emission path in the codebase), so it provably synchronizes ALL 64 threads / BOTH subgroups, and WorkgroupMemory semantics make the staged a_tile/b_tile writes visible cross-subgroup. The post-staging barrier is therefore load-bearing for the cross-subgroup stage->read dependency. The race in probe #1 is correctly closed by the design.
central_hazard_confirmations.per_subgroup_coopmat_validity: VALID per spec, CONTINGENT on real-GPU proof. VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix ops are Subgroup-scoped (coopmat.rs:67 Scope::Subgroup=3); in a 2-subgroup workgroup each 32-lane subgroup independently runs its own coopmat_load/mul_add/store on its own lanes — no cross-subgroup coopmat sharing. The design keeps the barrier and all coopmat ops at top level in control flow that is UNIFORM across the whole workgroup; sg_id (= local_x/sg_size, uniform within each subgroup because all 32 lanes of a subgroup share the same local_x/sg_size quotient) feeds ONLY index arithmetic (b read offset sg_id*32, C col base block_col*64+sg_id*32), never a branch around the barrier or a coopmat op. No subgroup-divergent control flow around coopmat ops => no coopmat-in-divergent-CF UB. This is sound, but per anti-pattern #9 it MUST be proven on a real >1-subgroup-per-workgroup GPU: AT-1743 (1 WG = 2 subgroups) and AT-1744 (4 WGs, 3 K-blocks) are the mandatory proofs and are correctly specified bit-exact (max_diff==0).
central_hazard_confirmations.subgroup_size_typed_skip: NOT TYPED-SKIPPED — THIS IS THE DEFECT. The design (EC-2, technical_spec portability note) claims the kernel 'stays portable' and 'is still CORRECT' on subgroup_size != 32 and reports occupancy 'honestly per device'. That correctness claim is FALSE (see CRITICAL-1). The precedent guard already exists in the codebase: dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 does `if ctx.subgroup_size() != 32 { skip (wave64 guard) }` and ctx.subgroup_size() is an available accessor. AT-1743/1744/AT-1750 are specified to typed-skip ONLY on CoopMatUnsupported/DeviceFeatureUnsupported (Lavapipe), with NO subgroup_size()==32 guard. On a wave64 or SIMD16 coopmat-capable device these tests would run the MISCOMPUTING kernel. The design must REPLACE the false 'still correct on any wave width' claim with an explicit subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip (mirroring AT-1510) on AT-1743/1744/AT-1750, and the .axc must document the hard N_SG=2 (sg_size==32) precondition.

critical_issues: CRITICAL-1 (the most dangerous hole): EC-2 / technical_spec portability note is FACTUALLY WRONG that subgroup_size != 32 stays correct. The MSG kernel's output coverage is hard-wired to exactly 2 subgroups by the constants 64 (b_tile width, grid divisor N/64) and sg_id*32 (B/C offset). (a) wave64 (sg_size=64): local_x in 0..63 => sg_id = local_x/64 = 0 for ALL 64 threads => only ONE subgroup runs => it writes C cols [block_col*64 .. +32) and reads b_tile cols [0..32), leaving C cols [block_col*64+32 .. +64) NEVER WRITTEN for every workgroup => HALF of C is garbage/zero. This is a silent miscompute, NOT a 'degrade to single-subgroup RB' (single-subgroup RB covers a 32-col region per WG with a 32-col grid; the MSG grid is 64-col, so the missing 32 cols are a real coverage hole). (b) SIMD16 (sg_size=16): sg_id in {0,1,2,3} => for sg_id=2,3 the B read offset sg_id*32 = 64/96 indexes OUT OF BOUNDS of the 64-wide b_tile (OOB shared read) AND writes C col base block_col*64 + 64/96 which lands in the NEXT workgroup's C region => overlapping/racing cross-workgroup C writes. Both are correctness-fatal, not occupancy notes. FIX: add an explicit subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip to AT-1743/1744/AT-1750 (mirror dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510), and rewrite EC-2 + the technical_spec portability paragraph + design_md_additions to state HONESTLY that the kernel REQUIRES sg_size==32 (N_SG=2) and is typed-skipped — NOT silently correct — on other wave widths. The .axc comment must state the sg_size==32 precondition.

CRITICAL-2: AT-1743 (M=32,N=64,K=32, grid (1,1,1) = ONE workgroup = 2 subgroups) does NOT independently prove the cross-subgroup barrier is load-bearing vs lockstep luck. On NVIDIA the 2 subgroups of an SM may execute in near-lockstep and mask a missing/weaker barrier (the 'NVIDIA-passes hazard' in probe #1). AT-1743 passing therefore does not by itself prove the barrier syncs subgroup 1's read against subgroup 0's write. MITIGATION ALREADY PRESENT: the barrier is provably workgroup-scope by construction (confirmation above) — correctness does not RELY on the test catching a wrong barrier because the design cannot emit a subgroup-scope barrier (no such path exists). So this is a WARNING-grade residual, not a blocker BY ITSELF, but the design should explicitly acknowledge that bit-exactness is guaranteed by the emitted workgroup-scope OpControlBarrier (verified by subgroup.rs:476 unit test), and AT-1743/1744 are the end-to-end confirmation, NOT the sole correctness guarantee. Add AT-1744's multi-K-block (3 blocks) WAR-barrier coverage to the justification — the second barrier (WAR before next k_block overwrites shared) is exercised only at K>16, so AT-1743 (K=32 => 2 K-blocks) and AT-1744 (K=48 => 3 K-blocks) DO exercise the WAR barrier; state this.
warnings: WARNING: a_iters/b_iters must divide evenly. a_block_size=512 over 64 threads = 8 iters; b_block_size=1024 over 64 threads = 16 iters — both exact. But the staging linear-index math (ei = iter*64 + t, ei in 0..a_block_size) assumes a_block_size and b_block_size are EXACT multiples of wg_threads(64). If a future @strategy assignment picks a non-multiple, threads at high ei would write OOB of a_tile/b_tile or leave gaps. The design should state the invariant a_block_size % wg_threads == 0 && b_block_size % wg_threads == 0 and (ideally) have AT-1745 assert it for the shipped assignment.

WARNING: b_tile coopmat_load stride is 64 (full b_tile width = N_SG*RB_N*16). The shipped matmul_rb_coopmat.axc uses stride 32 for its 32-wide b_tile. The MSG kernel doubles the b_tile to 64 wide and reads two 16-col bands per subgroup at offsets sg_id*32 and sg_id*32+16, stride 64. This is sound (each coopmat_load reads a 16x16 tile with row-stride 64 from a column-band of a 16x64 shared region), but it is a NEW shared-layout/stride combination not previously exercised; AT-1743 MUST use the non-symmetric fixture (A in {1..4}, B in {1..3}) so a swapped sg_id offset or wrong stride produces max_diff != 0. The design correctly specifies the non-symmetric fixture — keep it; do NOT substitute a symmetric one.

WARNING: occupancy at 256 (EC-6): msg grid is (4,8,1)=32 WGs of 64 threads. The design honestly predicts a possible 256 regression. Acceptable since no ratio is asserted and the single-subgroup RB bench is retained for A/B at every size.

WARNING (probe #4b): C output coverage of the 2 subgroups — subgroup 0 writes cols [block_col*64 .. +32), subgroup 1 writes [block_col*64+32 .. +64): DISTINCT, no overlap, no gap, exactly tiling the 64-col WG region. CONFIRMED disjoint AND complete for sg_size==32. (Only breaks for sg_size != 32 — CRITICAL-1.) The non-symmetric AT-1743 fixture would catch a swapped sg_id offset (subgroup 1 reading subgroup 0's columns).
principle_violations: VIOLATION (honesty, anti-pattern spirit): EC-2 and the technical_spec portability paragraph assert the non-32-subgroup result is 'still CORRECT' / 'bit-exactness holds regardless'. This is not honest — it is wrong (CRITICAL-1). 'Reported honestly per device' is contradicted by the absence of any per-device subgroup-size check. Honesty requires either typed-skipping non-32 (chosen fix) or a runtime predication that actually covers all columns (out of scope). The TFLOPS honesty (no asserted ratio, competitive only if pct>=25.0, durable-builtin framing) is otherwise sound and acceptable.
spirv_concerns: OK: local_invocation_id() lowering mirrors gid() exactly — buffers.rs emit_gid_variable (241-278) is the template: u32 -> vec3 u32 -> Input pointer -> OpVariable Input -> OpDecorate BuiltIn. The new LocalInvocationIdVar/emit_local_invocation_id_variable using BuiltIn::LocalInvocationId is structurally identical and emits NO capability (LocalInvocationId is core Shader). body.rs emit_gid_component (1991-2012) OpLoad vec3u32 + OpCompositeExtract by LITERAL axis is the template for emit_local_invocation_id_component. CONFIRMED no new OpCapability/OpExtension needed.

OK: interface list — emit.rs:397-411 builds the OpEntryPoint interface from Input-class vars (gid + subgroup invoc/size). Adding local_id_var.var_id here when emitted is correct for SPIR-V 1.3 (Input class must be listed). AT-1741 asserting the var is in the interface list is the right check.

CONCERN (minor): the design says 'emit ONLY when body_uses_local_invocation_id (opt-in), NOT on buffer presence like gid'. This is fine, but the body-scanner (body_uses_local_invocation_id) MUST recurse into ALL expression positions including loop bounds, shared-write indices, and nested binops where local_invocation_id(0) appears (the MSG kernel uses it as the cooperative-staging thread index t = local_invocation_id(0u32) inside staging loop index expressions, AND as sg_id numerator). If the scanner under-covers, the var is not emitted and emit_local_invocation_id_component hits the None branch => BodyCodegenError (compile failure, not UB — acceptable but the scanner must mirror body_uses_gid's full traversal, emit.rs:457-529). AT-1741 only tests a trivial kernel; ADD an AT-1745-adjacent assertion that matmul_msg_coopmat.axc actually emits the LocalInvocationId var (it must, since it calls the builtin).
vendor_concerns: Intel Arc (SIMD8/16/32, variable): SIMD16 => 4 subgroups => OOB shared read + cross-WG C overlap (CRITICAL-1b). MUST typed-skip on subgroup_size()!=32.

AMD (wave64 default; wave32 via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control): wave64 => 1 subgroup => half-C uncomputed (CRITICAL-1a). wave32 (if forced) => 2 subgroups => correct. MUST typed-skip on subgroup_size()!=32 (the kernel does not request a required subgroup size).
NVIDIA (wave32): sg_size=32 => N_SG=2 => correct. This is the only validated target. AT-1743/1744 run here.
Apple/MoltenVK: no VK_KHR_cooperative_matrix => CoopMatUnsupported typed-skip (already covered).

NOTE: the kernel could instead REQUEST a fixed subgroup size via VK_EXT_subgroup_size_control (requiredSubgroupSize=32) at pipeline creation — that would make it correct on wave64/SIMD16 hardware that supports the control. The design does NOT do this and need not for M3.3d; but then it MUST typed-skip non-32. Choose one; the design currently does NEITHER (the bug).
missing_tests: MUST ADD: subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip guard to AT-1743, AT-1744, AT-1750 (mirror dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510 wave64 guard). Without it these tests miscompute on non-32 coopmat GPUs.

MUST TEST (already specified, keep): AT-1742 local_id_probe out[g*64+l]==l on Lavapipe AND NVIDIA — exact-integer GPU oracle proving LocalInvocationId (NOT GlobalInvocationId) is returned. GOOD: 4 workgroups * 64 threads means out[g*64+l] tests that the value REPEATS per workgroup (0..63), which distinguishes local from global id — a global id would give g*64+l, not l. This is the correct discriminating oracle.

summary: The two BIGGEST concurrency hazards are CLEAN. (1) The cross-subgroup shared-memory barrier is provably WORKGROUP-scope: emit_workgroup_barrier (subgroup.rs:285-301) emits OpControlBarrier scope=2 (Workgroup) + semantics 0x108 (AcquireRelease|WorkgroupMemory), unit-tested at subgroup.rs:476, and there is no subgroup-scope barrier emission path to accidentally use — so all 64 threads/both subgroups sync and staged shared writes are cross-subgroup-visible. (2) Per-subgroup coopmat is valid: coopmat ops are Subgroup-scoped, each 32-lane subgroup runs its own block, sg_id is uniform-per-subgroup and feeds only index arithmetic (no divergent control flow around coopmat/barrier), with AT-1743/1744 (non-symmetric fixture, max_diff==0, 1 WG=2 subgroups and 4 WGs/3 K-blocks) as the mandatory real-GPU proofs. The local_invocation_id() builtin Part A is sound: it mirrors gid() exactly (buffers.rs:241-278 / body.rs:1991-2012 templates), adds NO new capability (LocalInvocationId is core Shader), is emitted only when used, and is added to the OpEntryPoint interface list; AT-1742 (out[g*64+l]==l, repeating per WG) is the correct discriminating oracle. THE BLOCKING DEFECT is portability honesty: EC-2 / the technical_spec portability note FALSELY claim the kernel 'stays correct' on subgroup_size != 32. It does not — wave64 leaves half of C uncomputed (sg_id always 0, second subgroup's columns never written) and SIMD16 produces OOB shared reads + cross-workgroup C-overwrite races. The codebase already has the right pattern (dispatch_matmul_tile.rs:231 AT-1510 'wave64 guard' subgroup_size()!=32 skip), but AT-1743/1744/AT-1750 omit it. NEEDS_REVISION: (a) add subgroup_size()==32 typed-skip to AT-1743/1744/AT-1750, (b) rewrite EC-2 + technical_spec portability + design_md to state the kernel REQUIRES sg_size==32 and is typed-skipped (not silently correct) elsewhere, (c) assert staging-size%wg_threads==0 + builtin-emission coverage in AT-1745, (d) state explicitly that bit-exactness is guaranteed by the emitted workgroup-scope barrier (not merely by AT-1743 possibly passing via NVIDIA lockstep). Fixes are small and localized (test guards + honest doc text); no codegen change needed beyond the already-correct builtin.
